sources.cite: Google Cloud documentation, Restrict resource locations (organization policy)
sources.note: Read through a summarizing fetch on 2026-11-18. The constraint is constraints/gcp.resourceLocations; value groups use the in: prefix, such as in:eu-locations; the restriction applies only to resources created after the policy is set and existing resources are not affected; policies can be set at the organization, folder or project.

brief.situation: You are the security engineer at Velden Health. Patient data for EU clinics must be stored only in EU locations. The eu-clinics folder has no location policy; residency was enforced by a review checklist. A new imaging pipeline created bucket gs://velden-imaging-raw in US multi-region last week and has written 3,100 scans there. The regulator's residency audit starts tomorrow at 09:00; today's evidence pack is due at 17:00.
handover: The pipeline's Terraform takes the bucket location from a variable that defaulted to US.
The eu-clinics folder holds 14 projects; none should create resources outside the EU.
howItWorks: The terminal shows each command's output; the diagram shows the eu-clinics folder, its projects, the imaging bucket in the US and the policy that should have stopped it.
Each command takes a minute or two; the clock moves only when you act or wait.
When you close, you write the record and explain your reasoning.

source.note: The evidence pack is due at 17:00, 210 minutes after the finding; it must show the data in the EU and a control that prevents a repeat.

enforce.label: Set gcp.resourceLocations to in:eu-locations on the folder, create an EU bucket, copy the scans and verify, point the pipeline at it, then delete the US bucket
enforce.available: not busy and (not fixed and not harmed)
enforce.why: Already done, or the system is down.

effects.output:
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud org-policies set-policy eu-locations.yaml   # folder eu-clinics: allowedValues in:eu-locations
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud storage buckets create gs://velden-imaging-raw-eu --location=EU --project=velden-imaging
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud storage cp -r gs://velden-imaging-raw/* gs://velden-imaging-raw-eu/ && gcloud storage ls -r gs://velden-imaging-raw-eu | wc -l   # 3,100
secops@cloudshell:~$ (pipeline variable bucket_location = EU; redeploy)
secops@cloudshell:~$ gcloud storage rm -r gs://velden-imaging-raw

effects.log: New resources in the folder can only be created in EU locations; the scans are in the EU bucket, verified by count, and the US copy is gone. The policy does not move existing resources, which is why the copy and delete are needed.

writeup.question: For the record: how EU data reached the US, what you changed in what order, and what prevents a repeat.

parts.label: How
parts.modelAnswer: eu-clinics had no gcp.resourceLocations policy, so the pipeline's Terraform default of US created a US bucket; only the pipeline accessed it.

parts.label: Order
parts.modelAnswer: Set in:eu-locations on the folder, created an EU bucket, copied and counted 3,100 scans, repointed the pipeline, then deleted the US bucket. Deleting first destroys the only copy; the policy alone does not move existing data.

parts.label: Prevention
parts.modelAnswer: No US default in the module, a CI check on plans, and the incident recorded for the DPO.

expertPath.text: No location policy; one US bucket; Terraform default US; only the pipeline read it.
Policy in:eu-locations; EU bucket; copy and count; repoint; delete US; module, CI, DPO record.

scansLost.headline: Move the data, then delete
scansLost.body: Residency is fixed by copying to an EU location, verifying, and only then deleting the out-of-region copy.

breachInEvidence.headline: Location policies do not move data
breachInEvidence.body: gcp.resourceLocations constrains new resources only; existing out-of-region data must be moved.

resident.headline: Good: a preventive control and a clean move
resident.body: You found no location policy and one US bucket, confirmed the cause and access, enforced in:eu-locations, moved and verified the data before deleting, and fixed the module and CI.

scoring.modelReasoning: Residency was enforced by a checklist, so the folder has no location policy and a Terraform default created a US bucket. Enforce gcp.resourceLocations with in:eu-locations on the folder, then move the data: create an EU bucket, copy and verify the 3,100 scans, repoint the pipeline, and only then delete the US bucket. Deleting first destroys the only copy; the policy alone does not touch existing resources. Then fix the module default and add a CI check.
